title: Felix Goff, Eugene Porter and other saxophonists in his band
summary: He names clarinet and sax players from his Desvigne and Ridgley days, including Felix Goff and tenor man Eugene Porter from Jackson, Mississippi.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yeah, right. See, he was playing with Sid and Desiree in a long time, he and my brother like Tom Johnson. But Tom's in California, too, a very good saxophone player. We had a saxophone, a clarinet player, was a very, very good, well, actually, if you've ever heard of it, by the name of Felix Goff. He used to play with Rizzly, when we were playing with Rizzly, old man Porter was playing who the former was, with Rizzly. And this boy named Felix Goff, he could play. Man, he could play some time. I thought, you know, sometime you might have run across him or his name. Is he still around? I don't know, I never heard of him for many years. He used to like to travel to circuses and shows, you know, like that rough, real rough life. He was rough, too, but he could play. Yeah. Another boy we got out of Jackson, Mississippi, Sam Tom, we picked up Brennan Montgomery. A boy called Eugene Porter. You ever hear of that?
Sam, you know, we talked to brother, you see.

What did he play? We played, we played tenor saxophone. And, we had to coach him to get up to take a course after he got the fright off him. He was tough, I'm telling you. And then he had McLaren, no time, no time, no time, I said a couple of months. He was sitting in the back of that plan and taking slow moves and things. Yeah, a couple of months. We had him at a bar on Brookhaven College, E.W. Brown. His daddy was over the Rabbitfoot Show one time. And Brookhaven, Brookhaven, a few miles from there, right in that neighborhood. But, yeah, he could play some time there. Very good.
